newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE cabinet quits, prime minister to form new one.
newsitem.headline: UAE cabinet quits, prime minister to form new one.

text.p: The government of the United Arab Emirates resigned on Sunday and President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan asked the prime minister to form a new cabinet, the official news agency WAM said.
The cabinet was formed in November 1990 following the death of Sheikh Rashid bin Said al-Maktoum, father of Prime Minister and Vice-President Sheikh Maktoum bin Rashid al-Maktoum.

Since then several ministers had been changed but this would be the first major reshuffle of the cabinet in the Gulf Arab state, a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), officials told Reuters.
"It is not a crisis resignation. Some ministers had resigned before, some are acting ministers...Sheikh Zaid had been talking about a new cabinet for some time," one official said.
The official agency said Sheikh Maktoum "presented the government's resignation" to Sheikh Zaid who asked the prime minister to form a new cabinet.
It gave no other details and it was not clear when the new cabinet would be announced.

The UAE, a federation of seven emirates, was formed in 1971 when Britain unilaterally withdrew its military protection from the impoverished Trucial States - Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Dubai, Fujairah, Ras al-Khaimah, Sharjah and Umm al-Quwain - which had subsisted on fishing, pearl-diving and trade.
The UAE is now one of the world's wealthiest countries with oil revenue of $9 billion a year and sufficient crude in the ground to last a century.

The highest federal authority in the UAE, where there are no political parties, is the Supreme Council composed of the rulers of the seven emirates. The Federal National Council, appointed by the rulers, has a consultative role.
